[2026-07-04_QUANTUM_SECTOR]  
Video Title: Will Quantum Stocks Decouple? Sourcing My Lagrangian Galaxy Orbits  
Video ID: tYGfwKDpUIM  
Quantum Stocks (QUANTUM_SECTOR) | Class: QUANTUM  

    Current Market Structure:  
    • The quantum sector is positioned in the golden breakout quadrant, defined by > median momentum and 90‑day return for the class is +59 %, with relative momentum at 100 % and trend quality high.  
    • 20‑week SMA sits at $48, 50‑week SMA at $48, and 200‑week SMA at $23, placing the current spot price of IONIC at $49 roughly 2× the 200‑week level.  
    • The sector’s average gravity risk is 51, and the galaxy status score ranges from 45–60, indicating a balanced rotation—neither deep accumulation nor euphoria.  

    Quantitative Valuation & Gravity:  
    • IONIC trades at $49, above its time‑weighted average price (TWAP) baseline of $20, yielding a 150 % premium.  
    • The negative‑2 σ floor places a fair‑value target at $85 if the growth trajectory continues.  
    • Annual return (since 2020) for IONIC is 108 % YoY with 100 % annual volatility; mean‑reversion probability is 31 %.  
    • Portfolio weightings: neutral quantum portfolio assigns 27 % to IONIC; risk‑averse reduces it to 21 %, while aggressive increases it to 33 %.  

    Target Floors & Trap Identifications:  
    • The negative‑2 σ floor at $85 signals a deep capitulation zone; the current price is $49, well above this floor but below the fair‑value target.  
    • The sector’s euphoria zone (40–60) and average gravity 51 suggest moderate risk, yet the neutral risk score of 58 places IONIC in the neutral territory—neither accumulation (66).  
    • Overextended periods (price once reached $6,768) are avoided by monitoring the dotted red line; current price is outside this overextended band.  
    • Value traps are flagged when the time‑weighted average price premium exceeds 150 %; LIN shows a 34 % premium but high risk due to large deviation from its TWAP.  

This concise, data‑dense summary captures all explicit tickers, numerical anchors, and risk metrics presented in the transcript.
